# Multiple accounts and servers on Android, with a local-only area — design of record

Decided with the maintainer on 2026-09-24. The Android app stops assuming one server and one
session. Each list belongs to exactly one **account**; an account is either a login on one server
or the phone's **local area**. The web client and the server do not change. This document is the
contract the step tickets implement; when it and the code disagree, the code is wrong.

## 1. Decisions

* **One list, one home.** A list is bound to the account it was created or received under. It
  never moves. Getting a list to another account means copying it (section 6), which creates a
  new, separate, one-member list there.
* **Local area** = an account with no server. Only shopping lists and checklists can live there;
  ledgers need accounts to name payers and are not offered. Nothing in it is backed up or shared,
  and the UI says so once, when the area is created.
* **Removing an account** keeps today's warning dialog and adds one sentence: lists you want to
  keep can be copied to the local area first (section 6). Nothing is copied automatically.
  Unpushed changes are warned about exactly as today.
* **Per-account "app too old".** A `426 client_outdated` from one server marks that account as
  outdated and disables it; the other accounts keep working. The app-wide update screen (T-244)
  stays for the case where every server account is outdated.
* **Server protocol floor.** The client refuses a server whose protocol is below
  `MIN_SERVER_PROTOCOL` when the account is added (read from `GET /app-version`, T-265). The
  server's protocol is stored per account for future feature gating. Rationale: today a newer
  client talking to an older server is silently accepted and the server drops unknown keys, e.g.
  a ledger `type` becomes an expense. Once the app is on F-Droid and strangers run their own
  servers, "stay compatible with older servers" is the client's job. There is one production
  instance today, so a breaking protocol change is still cheap now and expensive later.
* **Silent before login (T-287) still holds:** the app contacts only a server whose URL the user
  typed and confirmed. The floor check is the first request to a new server.
* **Portability.** The data layer is extracted into a `:core` module with no Android on its
  classpath (B0) so it can later become Kotlin Multiplatform and serve an iPhone port. Compose
  UI, Hilt, WorkManager and the Keystore stay in `:app` behind interfaces.
* **Parity exception.** AGENTS.md's "both clients, always" rule does not apply to account
  management: the web client is served by one server and is always one account there. Android
  strings for it still exist in all nine locales; `crossClient.test.ts` pairs by identical
  English, so Android-only strings pass unchanged. Recorded in AGENTS.md by B2.
* **No server change.** Everything here is client-side. The invite link already carries the
  server host, which is how the app picks the account (section 5).

## 2. Data model (Room, `:core`)

New table `accounts`:

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | local UUID, primary key; never the server's account id |
| `kind` | `server` \| `local` |
| `serverUrl` | normalised with trailing slash; null for `local` |
| `accountId`, `email`, `isAdmin` | as the server reports them; null for `local` |
| `label` | display name; defaults to the server host |
| `signedIn` | false after a 401 or a logout that kept unpushed rows (today's `mirrorAccountId` case) |
| `outdated` | set by 426, cleared by a successful request |
| `serverProtocol` | from `/app-version` at add time and refreshed on the update check |
| `syncCursor`, `defaultCurrency`, `ignoredInviteIdsJson`, `allowSelfSignedCerts` | today's per-session state, now per account |
| `sortOrder` | user order on the overview |

Unique on (`serverUrl`, `accountId`). `lists` gets `accountId` (FK, indexed); items reach their
account through the list. The bearer token is not in Room: it stays in the Keystore-backed
EncryptedSharedPreferences, keyed by the local account id.

**Migration** (schema 9): create `accounts`; if `SessionStore` holds an account id, or only a
`mirrorAccountId`, insert one `server` row from it and `ServerConfig.serverUrl`, copy cursor,
currency, ignored invites and the self-signed flag into it, tag every list with it, and move the
token under the new key. `signedIn` = whether a token exists. Without either id there are no
lists (T-257 wipes on account change) and nothing is inserted. `ServerConfig.serverUrl` and the
single-session keys are then unused and removed. The device id stays global.

## 3. Runtime shape (`:core`)

* `AccountRegistry`: the accounts as a Flow plus add/remove/update; the only writer of the table.
* `AccountSession` per server account: its API client (base URL, token, protocol header, error
  interceptor), sync cursor and `SyncStatus`. Built lazily and cached by account id; dropped on
  remove. 401 and 426 are delivered per session and set `signedIn=false` / `outdated=true` on that
  row instead of today's process-wide `SessionEvents`.
* `SyncEngine.syncNow()` runs every signed-in, non-outdated server account in turn; one account's
  failure does not stop the others. The aggregated status the UI shows is "worst of" the accounts
  plus per-account detail on the Accounts screen. `SyncWorker` is unchanged apart from calling
  this. The local account is never synced.
* Repos: creation takes an account id; everything by list id stays as it is, the list knows its
  account. `deleteSyncedRows()` and the 410 re-base act on one account's lists.
* `UpdateChecker` asks each server account's `/app-version`; the update offer is the newest.
  Collaborator notifications carry the account label when more than one account exists.
* Platform interfaces owned by `:core`, implemented in `:app`: `SecretStore` (tokens),
  `BackgroundSync` (WorkManager), `Clock`, `DeviceId`. Hilt wiring lives in `:app` only.

## 4. Screens (B2, B3)

* **Start screen** replaces the login screen on a phone with no account: Sign in · Register ·
  Use without an account. Sign in/Register are today's login form (server URL, email, password,
  T-276 registration check after the URL is confirmed). "Use without an account" creates the
  local area, shows the one-time note, and opens the overview.
* **Accounts** (Settings → Accounts): one row per account with label, email or "On this phone",
  and state (signed in · signed out — tap to sign in again · app too old for this server · local).
  Actions: add account (today's login form), add local area (when none), rename label, reorder,
  remove (warning dialog, section 1). The local area can be removed only when it holds no lists.
* **Overview**: one account → exactly today's screen. Several → sections with the account label
  as header, in `sortOrder`, the local area last; a small indicator on each card (host initial or
  phone glyph) so a card is placeable when the list is scrolled. Pending invites appear in the
  section of the account they were sent to. The "New list" dialog gets an account picker when
  there is more than one; default is the account of the last opened list. Under the local area
  the ledger kind is not shown.
* **List screen**: unchanged. The app bar subtitle shows the account label only with several
  accounts.
* **Settings** that are really per account (default currency, notification preference) move
  under the account row; app-wide ones (theme, locale, show checked) stay.
* Nine locales for every new string; no web change.

## 5. Invite links

`/invite/<token>` opens the app as today. The link's host is matched against the server
accounts' hosts: one match → redeem there; several (same host, several logins) → pick; none →
the add-account form pre-filled with that server, then redeem. `PendingInviteHolder` remembers the
token across the login.

## 6. Copy across accounts (B4)

Today's snapshot copy (T-63, `ListsRepo.copy`) gains a target account. In List properties,
"Copy" opens a picker when more than one account exists ("Copy to: <account>"); the result is a
new one-member list under the target with a fresh id, fresh field clocks, `updated_by` = this
device, items and category order copied, the name suffixed as today. Ledgers are not copyable
across accounts (the participants are accounts of one server); the picker shows only the source
account for them. Copying into a server account makes the new rows dirty and they push on the
next sync; copying into the local area makes them local forever.

## 7. Staging

| step | ticket | scope |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | core module, move-only | `:core` JVM module, no Android on its classpath, tests unchanged |
| B1 | multi-account data layer | section 2 + 3, migration, protocol floor; UI still single-account |
| B2 | accounts in the UI | section 4 without the local area, section 5, AGENTS.md parity note |
| B3 | local area | section 1 local rules, start screen option, first-run note |
| B4 | copy across accounts | section 6 |
| B5 | core goes multiplatform | Ktor instead of Retrofit/OkHttp, `javax.inject` out of core, iOS target compiles |
| — | F-Droid readiness | separate design, blocked until the maintainer picks it up |

Each step ships on its own; B1 is invisible to the user and must leave an upgraded install
behaving exactly as before.
title: Multiple accounts and servers on Android, with a local-only area (design)
